title: Equestrian equipment: overview
description: Equestrian equipment essentials: helmet, boots. Helmets are certified; boots protect the leg. The right gear does three things: keeps you safe, lets you perform, and lasts. title: Protective gear

title: Maintenance
d: Maintain Equestrian gear: clean, dry, inspect, store.
definition: Maintain Equestrian gear: clean, dry, inspect, store.
description: Maintenance for Equestrian equipment: clean after use, dry fully before storage, inspect before every session, store out of sun and damp. Helmets are certified; boots protect the leg. A five-minute routine doubles gear life. Keep a small repair kit — tape, laces, patches — because failures happen at venues, not at home.

title: Fitting guide
d: Fit Equestrian gear properly: the performance multiplier.
definition: Fit Equestrian gear properly: the performance multiplier.
description: Fitting Equestrian gear: the difference between good and great equipment is usually fit. Helmets are certified; boots protect the leg. Get fitted by someone who knows the sport, re-check fit as young athletes grow, and never borrow safety gear. If it moves, pinches, or distracts, it does not fit.

title: Safety standards

definition: Equestrian gear must meet certification standards.

title: Youth gear
d: Young Equestrian athletes need sized-down, not dumbed-down, gear.
definition: Young Equestrian athletes need sized-down, not dumbed-down, gear.
description: Youth Equestrian gear: sized for growing bodies, never adult hand-me-downs that do not fit. Helmets are certified; boots protect the leg. Kids outgrow gear fast — buy adjustable where possible and check fit monthly. Never compromise on helmets or protection to save money; skimp on the bag, not the brain bucket.

title: Budget guide
d: Equip for Equestrian at any budget: spend on safety first.
definition: Equip for Equestrian at any budget: spend on safety first.
description: Budgeting Equestrian gear: spend first on protection and fit, then on the implement, last on accessories. Helmets are certified; boots protect the leg. Good used gear beats bad new gear for non-safety items. Plan the yearly replacement cycle so costs never surprise you mid-season.

title: Rules on equipment
